+=== camel-jbang-mcp - the security audit is part of camel_dependency_check, and four tools are removed
+The `camel_dependency_security_audit` MCP tool is removed. `camel_dependency_check` takes the same arguments and
+returns the audit in its new `security` section: the published CVE advisories of each declared artifact at the
+project's Camel version, `reachable` when routes are given, the advisories that name no component as
+`uncheckedAdvisories`, and `clean`. When the `pom.xml` sets no Camel version, the check uses the `camelVersion`
+argument, else lists every advisory of the declared components, and says so in `security.warnings`. The summary
+counts the vulnerable artifacts in `vulnerableArtifactCount` and in `totalIssueCount` when the Camel version is
+known, so a project with a known CVE is no longer reported `healthy`.
+These MCP tools are removed, with no replacement tool:
+* `camel_error_diagnose`, from both MCP servers (`camel mcp` and `camel tui --mcp`), as it was one of the authoring
+  tools they share: it matched an error against a fixed list of exceptions. `camel_get_errors` returns the failed
+  exchanges of an integration with their stack traces, and `camel_get_log` its log. The exception reference data
+  stays available as the `camel://error/exception-catalog` and `camel://error/exception/\{name}` resources of
+* `camel_ai_pipeline_scaffold`: the route it returned referred to beans it did not define. Build such a route with
+  `camel_catalog_doc` and the documentation of the AI components.
+* `camel_route_cost_estimate`: its prices were written into the code and did not follow the provider prices.
+* `camel_route_test_scaffold`: it wrote a JUnit 5 test class. The Camel CLI runs Citrus tests: `camel test init`
+  creates one, and `camel test run` runs it.
